title: The Fat Transition
prompt:
**Scenario.** dp[i] = min over j < i of dp[j] + (a[i] + b[j])² — note the square spans both i and j. n = 200000. What is the true situation?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Prefix-min fusion works: keep min of dp[j] + b[j]

**B)** The square entangles i and j (expands to a[i]² + 2·a[i]·b[j] + b[j]²); the cross term 2·a[i]·b[j] makes the best j depend on a[i] — a Li Chao/convex-hull structure, not a plain prefix min

**C)** DP is impossible here; use Dijkstra

**D)** Sort by a[i] + b[j] and take the first

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: Expanding the square exposes the entangled cross term: the optimal j depends on −2·a[i], which is exactly the line-query pattern (Li Chao tree / CHT). Plain prefix-min fusion would silently answer the wrong question.
